content.text:
Yes — your fork, your rules. No need to wait for upstream review on anything.

Six agents are running in parallel right now on `feat/cloudflare-deployment`:

| Agent | Work |
|---|---|
| Config + R2 stores | `deploymentPlatform` config axis (already landed — you can see it in the system notes), R2 RunLogStore, R2 WorkspaceOpLogStore, boot wiring |
| Route group 1 | `companies.ts`, `agents.ts`, `projects.ts`, `goals.ts` → Handler shape |
| Route group 2 | `issues.ts`, `issue-tree-control.ts`, `approvals.ts`, `costs.ts`, `activity.ts`, `dashboard.ts` |
| Route group 3 | `auth.ts`, `user-profiles.ts`, `sidebar-*.ts`, `inbox-dismissals.ts`, `instance-settings.ts`, `routines.ts`, `llms.ts` |
| Route group 4 | `environments.ts`, `execution-workspaces.ts`, `secrets.ts`, `assets.ts`, `adapters.ts`, `plugins.ts` |
| CF services | `SidecarClient`, `CfCompanySkillsService`, `CfAgentInstructionsService` + `api.ts` update |

When they finish I'll commit everything and give you the full picture of what's done vs. what's been marked with `// TODO(cloudflare):` for the next phase (plugin system process model is the only thing genuinely requiring a separate architectural design pass).
